review_cost.rationale: Approve-with-nits: nothing structural needs rework; the asks are typing, test coverage, and a handful of robustness tweaks.

findings.issue: The API layer is untyped (api<T = any>, apiUrl<T = any>), so every view relies on ~20 `any` casts (e.g. app/src/views/pokemon.tsx:224-240) and silent property mistakes would go unnoticed by `tsc --noEmit`.
findings.suggestion: Define interfaces for the PokeAPI resources used (species, pokemon, move, ability, type, generation) and annotate the call sites, or at minimum type the fields views actually read.

findings.issue: The app ships no tests at all (0 test files) even though it contains pure, high-value logic: sortRows with its missing-values-last rule (pokemon.tsx:36-47), typeCoverage multipliers (team.tsx:88-107), parseHomeQuery clamping (home.tsx:21-31), readTeam dedup/truncation (team.tsx:15-26).
findings.suggestion: Add a lightweight runner (e.g. vitest or node:test) with unit tests for these helpers; they encode the spec's subtlest rules.

findings.issue: Team cookie value is `names.join(',')`; comma is not a legal cookie-octet under RFC 6265, so a strict proxy or cookie parser between client and server could mangle or reject the team.
findings.suggestion: Join with '.' or '|' (never present in species names), or store a JSON array.

findings.issue: serveStatic({ root: './dist' }) resolves relative to process.cwd(), so `npm start` works only when launched from app/; a supervisor or different working directory breaks all static assets.
findings.suggestion: Derive the path from the module location (e.g. new URL('../static', import.meta.url)) or document the cwd requirement.

findings.issue: fetch() to the API has no AbortSignal or timeout; a hung upstream stalls every page render with no error page.
findings.suggestion: Use AbortSignal.timeout(...) (or a small wrapper) and let the failure surface to the existing onError handler.

findings.issue: mainTypes() exposes the raw `record: any` alongside the curated {name, label}, so views depend on raw API JSON shape (team.tsx:68-69, data.ts:70) — a leaky data-layer boundary that also spreads the `any` typing.
findings.suggestion: Have the data module expose only what views need (e.g. precomputed damage-relation sets or a typed record).

findings.issue: POST /team/add/:name writes whatever path segment it receives into the persistent cookie without checking it names a real species.
findings.suggestion: Validate against the species list (or at least an /^[a-z0-9-]+$/ shape check) before writing the cookie.

findings.issue: Conditional `disabled` via attribute spread is awkward and hides intent compared to the framework's native boolean handling.
findings.suggestion: Write `disabled={disabled || undefined}` — hono/jsx renders it as a boolean attribute on 4.13.

summary: A genuinely idiomatic Hono 4 + htmx 2 app on the latest stable versions, with an unusually careful partial/full-page split (Vary, HX-Push-Url, history-restore) and a team-builder feature that follows the existing conventions exactly. I'd merge it after one round of nits: type the API payloads, add unit tests for the spec's subtle pure helpers, and fix the cookie delimiter and cwd-dependent static root. Overall 4: approve with minor changes.
